text:
alex: Heads up — we have ~$120k in promo credits tied to project 'stone' expiring in 11 days (us-west1/CUSTOMER_PROD). Can we re-route any of that to Reserved/Dedicated commits or apply to upcoming invoices? cc @sophia @raj :eyes:

sophia: Is that promo actually transferable? Some promos are cloud-provider-only, others are project-level. I can check the usage profile, but if it's region-locked to us-west1 it might only cover hosted usage there.

raj: From the finance side, the contract credits we control are different from cloud promos. If this is a third-party promo (cloud vendor) we can't extend it, but we *can* prioritize spending it by shifting workloads. Any concrete spend hotspots? :thinking:

ops-bot: Auto-report: last 30d GPU spend for project 'stone' in us-west1 = $94,200. Forecast for next 11 days = $38,400 (based on current trend). Idle GPU reserve pool usage ~12%.

alex: Good to know. Thought: move non-latency-critical batch jobs (model evaluation, nightly retrain) from us-east1 to us-west1 for next 10 days to consume credits. Also propose applying any remaining promo to invoice INV-2026-03-18 if allowed.

sophia: That could work. Two constraints: 1) capacity — can we provision extra preemptible/spot GPUs in us-west1? 2) networking — data egress between regions might offset savings. If it's all within same cloud provider and project, egress should be minimal.

ops-bot: Current us-west1 spare capacity: 48 preemptible v100 slots, 6 reserved slots free in Dedicated pool. Net throughput enough for most batch jobs.

sophia: Ok. I’ll schedule a short maintenance window to shift batch pipelines — low-risk. Will update cron configs and autoscaler.

raj: I asked billing-bot to attempt a dry-run application of promo credits to the invoice. If it's a cloud vendor promo, it usually shows up as a discount line, not a line-item credit we can reassign.

billing-bot: Billing query result:
```
SELECT invoice_id, vendor_promo_code, amount_applied, expires_at FROM billing_export
WHERE project = 'stone' AND amount_applied > 0 ORDER BY expires_at ASC LIMIT 10;
-- returns: INV-2026-02-01, PROMO-XYZ-2025, $120,000, 2026-03-29
```

alex: So promo is vendor-tied and will auto-apply to eligible charges in that project/region until 3/29. We should plan workload moves to make sure eligible charges occur in us-west1 before then.

sophia: Quick checklist from infra side:
- update batch pipeline region to us-west1 (will run tonight)
- ensure model cache warmup so no cold-start surge costs
- throttle retries to avoid unnecessary token usage

raj: Finance checklist:
- confirm promo is not linked to an account-level setting that disallows usage for Dedicated reserved capacity (I suspect it won't apply to vendor-managed reserved purchases)
- evaluate whether applying remaining company-controlled contract credits to next invoice is better if promo can't be used for Dedicated purchase

alex: If promo can't cover Dedicated purchase, we can still use promo for hosted/ephemeral usage and use contract credits for the Dedicated commit. That keeps capacity predictable and uses both pools.

billing-bot: Quick note: vendor promos typically do NOT apply to committed-savings/reserved purchases (depends on vendor). See vendor T&C s.4.b. Recommend we assume they won't, unless we get a support exception.

raj: I'll open a ticket with vendor support now asking: "Can PROMO-XYZ-2025 be applied to a one-time Dedicated capacity reservation in us-west1 for project 'stone'?" Will paste the support case here when created.

alex: Thanks — if support says no, we proceed with schedule to shift batch jobs and consume promo on hosted usage, and use contract credits for Dedicated. If yes, we may move some of the Dedicated commit forward to lock in lower rates.

sophia: One more operational note: if we accelerate Dedicated commit, we need to check quota increment lead time in us-west1. Some quotas take 48-72h to update.

ops-bot: Quota note: Dedicated GPU quota increase request in us-west1 typically ~36h median; current available within project = 60 GPUs, desired for commit bump = 120 GPUs.

raj: Support case created: CASE-9342 -> "Promo applicability to Dedicated reservation". Case link: https://vendor.support.example/cases/9342.

alex: Great. I'll ping product teams to pause any non-critical large jobs in us-east1 and route them to us-west1 after sophia's go-ahead. Let's reconvene in ~12h or when support responds. :thumbsup:
